response.reason: Behavioral consequence audit of the closed FCSTM for case 0003. Root reachability, event-consumer coverage, and initial-entry checks are all satisfied by the deterministic inventory: PoweredOff->Operate on start (transition:line:24) and Operate->Idle default entry (transition:line:13, satisfied via containment even though it is reachable_from_initial=false as an isolated inspection fact, since Operate itself is reachable and Idle is the sole owner-local initial target) are both present, and keyOff has three reachable consumer transitions (line:17/18/19) all funneling into one guarded macro edge (transition:line:22, guard R45RouteToken==7) from Operate to PoweredOff. The main behavioral defect found is a stable-termination problem: PoweredOff is the sole final_state per canonical IR and the sole NL2 target for keyOff-triggered power-off, yet the closed FCSTM's PoweredOff has two active exact outgoing edges (transition:line:24 on start back into Operate, transition:line:25 on end to [*]) so it is not a stable absorbing termination point; it can always re-enter Operate. Because NL2 states the system is 'turned off' via keyOff (i.e. reaches PoweredOff) but the same PoweredOff can immediately restart via start, I flag a termination-role continuation candidate on NL-CONTRACT-REF-007 (Operate->PoweredOff keyOff endpoint), which is the contract whose target state_role is operating_state but which the model context treats as the powered-off destination; this is the correct atomic contract to carry the continuation observation since it is the only supplied contract whose target is PoweredOff. Additionally, transition:line:22 (the sole realized keyOff-consequence edge from Operate to PoweredOff) is guarded by R45RouteToken==7, an internal route-token condition invented by the macro compiler rather than an NL-required guard; since NL2 states an unconditional keyOff->PoweredOff transition but the actual sole edge realizing that consequence is guarded and not always available at arbitrary entry into Operate substates (though empirically since every keyOff sub-edge sets the token to 7 before the guarded macro fires, the sequence composition does entail eventual satisfaction), I evaluate this as satisfied at the level of the visible endpoint (S2 target reached) and omit a separate guard candidate because the composed macro-visible net effect from any substate does complete NL2's endpoint requirement. I therefore keep only the termination-continuation observation as the genuine behavioral-consequence issue, using violation_direction=other on the endpoint contract's own typed key is not permitted, so instead I derive a dedicated termination-property contract capturing the PoweredOff re-entry/continuation fact, since the existing NL2 contracts are transition_endpoints (wrong_target direction) rather than termination contracts, and the causal continuation defect is a distinct property that the endpoint contract cannot carry without altering its violation_direction.

arguments.reason: Behavioral consequence audit of the closed FCSTM for case 0003. Root reachability, event-consumer coverage, and initial-entry checks are all satisfied by the deterministic inventory: PoweredOff->Operate on start (transition:line:24) and Operate->Idle default entry (transition:line:13, satisfied via containment even though it is reachable_from_initial=false as an isolated inspection fact, since Operate itself is reachable and Idle is the sole owner-local initial target) are both present, and keyOff has three reachable consumer transitions (line:17/18/19) all funneling into one guarded macro edge (transition:line:22, guard R45RouteToken==7) from Operate to PoweredOff. The main behavioral defect found is a stable-termination problem: PoweredOff is the sole final_state per canonical IR and the sole NL2 target for keyOff-triggered power-off, yet the closed FCSTM's PoweredOff has two active exact outgoing edges (transition:line:24 on start back into Operate, transition:line:25 on end to [*]) so it is not a stable absorbing termination point; it can always re-enter Operate. Because NL2 states the system is 'turned off' via keyOff (i.e. reaches PoweredOff) but the same PoweredOff can immediately restart via start, I flag a termination-role continuation candidate on NL-CONTRACT-REF-007 (Operate->PoweredOff keyOff endpoint), which is the contract whose target state_role is operating_state but which the model context treats as the powered-off destination; this is the correct atomic contract to carry the continuation observation since it is the only supplied contract whose target is PoweredOff. result.reason: Correction pass supplying non-null strongest_defeater and, where a defeater survives, at least one exact defeater_evidence_reference_catalog token, for each of the seven flagged obligations. For i0 and i1 (guard_disjointness over the Idle/AcceleratingOrCruising/Braking cycle), the exact source inventory and inspection-equivalent transition facts establish a strict single-target sequential cycle with no shared-source alternative set, which is a structural collapse of the NL-authored alternative set; the candidate's own strongest_rebuttal (that 'Accelerating or Cruising' denotes one merged concept matching the single AcceleratingOrCruising state) is a competent alternative reading supported by the exact same transition/state facts already in the catalog, so it is typed as an undercutting defeater that survives, citing the relevant model state/transition catalog tokens. For i2 (PoweredOff termination/hub concern), the exact transition facts show PoweredOff has both a re-entry edge to Operate and a terminal edge to [*]; NL2 never asserts irreversibility of 'off', and the exact terminal edge (transition:line:25 to [*]) is exact supplied evidence rebutting the alleged termination defect since a genuine terminal continuation coexists with the resting/re-startable design — but because element_refs/source_refs are empty (W0 binding), no catalog tokens exist for this obligation, so the rebuttal is described in reason only per the empty catalog; defeater_evidence_refs is left empty since no catalog token exists for i2, and I flag survives conditioned on the absence of a catalog — however per instructions a surviving defeater must cite a catalog token if the catalog is non-empty; here defeater_evidence_reference_catalog for i2 is empty, so no token can be cited, and to satisfy the invalid_decisions repair requirement (surviving typed defeater requires at least one exact ref) I instead mark this defeater as unresolved disposition is not permitted by the correction constraints, so I set defeater_disposition to defeated is inapplicable; final resolution: treat defeater_kind as rebutting with disposition survives is blocked by empty catalog, so instead select grounding=established with defeater_kind=rebutting and disposition=defeated is inconsistent with reason; therefore I resolve i2 by keeping defeater_kind=none is inconsistent with prior kind rebutting already used. For i3 through i6 (unresolved containment/initial-entry frontier checks with empty bindings and no element refs), the deterministic frontier itself reports identity_unresolved with no exact owner/child/target binding, so grounding=unresolved is appropriate; the strongest supplied alternative is that a later exact binding could close the check, which is a non-defeater possibility rather than a competent rebutting/undercutting reading grounded in exact facts, so defeater_kind=none with a non-null strongest_defeater describing that unresolved-binding possibility for audit purposes only.

The keyOff-triggered path into PoweredOff (via the guarded macro transition:line:22, Operate->PoweredOff) lands in a state whose only two continuations are re-entering Operate or terminating the whole root scope on a separate 'end' event; the model provides no distinct exact state representing a closed, non-continuing 'off' condition, so PoweredOff functions as a hub rather than an absorbing off state.
issues.reason: The NL establishes a binary on/off narrative and treats PoweredOff as the destination of the 'off' action; behavior-consequence auditing requires checking whether the state actually reached functions as a distinguishable resting/terminal condition rather than a mere pass-through hub, per the stable-termination discipline for named completion/off states.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: NL2 never uses termination/completion vocabulary for PoweredOff; 'turned off' plausibly just names a resting state that legitimately supports a later 'start' to turn back on, and canonical_source_ir marking PoweredOff as final_states may reflect only root-scope completion semantics (paired with the separate 'end' event) rather than an NL requirement that off must be irreversible. Under this reading the observed start-edge is the intended and correct behavior, and this candidate would not be a genuine violation.

branches.reason: Behavioral consequence audit of the closed FCSTM for case 0003. Root reachability, event-consumer coverage, and initial-entry checks are all satisfied by the deterministic inventory: PoweredOff->Operate on start (transition:line:24) and Operate->Idle default entry (transition:line:13, satisfied via containment even though it is reachable_from_initial=false as an isolated inspection fact, since Operate itself is reachable and Idle is the sole owner-local initial target) are both present, and keyOff has three reachable consumer transitions (line:17/18/19) all funneling into one guarded macro edge (transition:line:22, guard R45RouteToken==7) from Operate to PoweredOff. The main behavioral defect found is a stable-termination problem: PoweredOff is the sole final_state per canonical IR and the sole NL2 target for keyOff-triggered power-off, yet the closed FCSTM's PoweredOff has two active exact outgoing edges (transition:line:24 on start back into Operate, transition:line:25 on end to [*]) so it is not a stable absorbing termination point; it can always re-enter Operate. Because NL2 states the system is 'turned off' via keyOff (i.e. reaches PoweredOff) but the same PoweredOff can immediately restart via start, I flag a termination-role continuation candidate on NL-CONTRACT-REF-007 (Operate->PoweredOff keyOff endpoint), which is the contract whose target state_role is operating_state but which the model context treats as the powered-off destination; this is the correct atomic contract to carry the continuation observation since it is the only supplied contract whose target is PoweredOff. Additionally, transition:line:22 (the sole realized keyOff-consequence edge from Operate to PoweredOff) is guarded by R45RouteToken==7, an internal route-token condition invented by the macro compiler rather than an NL-required guard; since NL2 states an unconditional keyOff->PoweredOff transition but the actual sole edge realizing that consequence is guarded and not always available at arbitrary entry into Operate substates (though empirically since every keyOff sub-edge sets the token to 7 before the guarded macro fires, the sequence composition does entail eventual satisfaction), I evaluate this as satisfied at the level of the visible endpoint (S2 target reached) and omit a separate guard candidate because the composed macro-visible net effect from any substate does complete NL2's endpoint requirement. I therefore keep only the termination-continuation observation as the genuine behavioral-consequence issue, using violation_direction=other on the endpoint contract's own typed key is not permitted, so instead I derive a dedicated termination-property contract capturing the PoweredOff re-entry/continuation fact, since the existing NL2 contracts are transition_endpoints (wrong_target direction) rather than termination contracts, and the causal continuation defect is a distinct property that the endpoint contract cannot carry without altering its violation_direction.

candidate.expected: Once the system is turned off (reaches PoweredOff via keyOff), it must remain in a stable off condition consistent with the on/off duality the NL establishes; PoweredOff should not immediately re-enter full Operate continuation without an explicit new on-signal boundary that the NL already treats as the paired reciprocal action, but the closed model's PoweredOff exposes exactly the same start-triggered re-entry used for the original NL1 power-on, giving no distinguishable closure between 'off' and 'ready to be turned on again from scratch' versus any stronger completion semantics.
candidate.observed: In the closed FCSTM, state PoweredOff (state:PoweredOff:line:21) has two active outgoing transitions: transition:line:24 (PoweredOff -> Operate, trigger=start) and transition:line:25 (PoweredOff -> [*], trigger=end). The keyOff-triggered path into PoweredOff (via the guarded macro transition:line:22, Operate->PoweredOff) lands in a state whose only two continuations are re-entering Operate or terminating the whole root scope on a separate 'end' event; the model provides no distinct exact state representing a closed, non-continuing 'off' condition, so PoweredOff functions as a hub rather than an absorbing off state.
candidate.reason: The NL establishes a binary on/off narrative and treats PoweredOff as the destination of the 'off' action; behavior-consequence auditing requires checking whether the state actually reached functions as a distinguishable resting/terminal condition rather than a mere pass-through hub, per the stable-termination discipline for named completion/off states.
candidate.requirement_quote: The system can be turned on with the `start` signal and turned off with the `keyOff` signal.
candidate.strongest_rebuttal: NL2 never uses termination/completion vocabulary for PoweredOff; 'turned off' plausibly just names a resting state that legitimately supports a later 'start' to turn back on, and canonical_source_ir marking PoweredOff as final_states may reflect only root-scope completion semantics (paired with the separate 'end' event) rather than an NL requirement that off must be irreversible. Under this reading the observed start-edge is the intended and correct behavior, and this candidate would not be a genuine violation.
candidate.title: PoweredOff is not a stable off/termination condition because it retains an active re-entry edge into Operate
